evidence: app/src/index.tsx:77-81 — ability route plus its import at index.tsx:13 must be deleted
app/src/views/details.tsx:53-78 — loadAbility/AbilityPage live in a file shared with moves and types
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:284-288 — Pokémon page hardcodes /abilities/<name> links, so removal requires editing an unrelated page to avoid dead links
app/src/views/layout.tsx:19-27 — nav has no Abilities link, so no nav edit needed
removability.rationale: Removing Abilities means a handful of scattered edits across three files rather than deleting a self-contained unit; the cross-page hardcoded links are the main snag.

evidence: app/src/data.ts:28 — spriteUrl is the single sprite-URL builder
app/src/views/components.tsx:25 — the only sprite render site, used by every card list (home.tsx:57, details.tsx:38,71,132)
app/src/api.ts:4-45 — base URL and all caching rules (FRESH_MS, cache map) in one module
app/src/data.ts:91 — cardsForPokemon centralizes the pokémon→species mapping used by move, ability and type pages
changeability.rationale: Most fixes land in one obvious function or module; only a fix needing Pokémon-record data would ripple through the Card producers.

evidence: app/src/api.ts → data.ts → views — clean one-directional layering; views import narrow helpers (Card, TypeInfo)
app/src/views/components.tsx:23 — route literal /pokemon/<name> duplicated with pokemon.tsx:178, details.tsx:86,146, home.tsx:19
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:57-64 — shared state (type label map) is passed explicitly as a parameter, not global
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:77-112 — loadMoves and MoveRow construction use untyped 'any' records, blurring the contract with the API layer
coupling.rationale: Structure is loosely coupled with clear seams, but URL strings are inlined in five places and untyped API records weaken module boundaries.

evidence: app/src/data.ts:89-100 — Card with optional types/note stretches across home, move, ability and type lists without flag parameters
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:122-192 — MoveTable filters columns for level-up vs other methods and generalizes sorting in sortRows
app/src/views/details.tsx:5-78 — Move and Ability pages share Section/Count/CardList but each repeats the effect-fallback expression inline (details.tsx:14, 65)
app/src/views/details.tsx:5-160 — moves, abilities and types bundled in one file, so an Items resource has no clean place to slot in
abstraction_design.rationale: The Card/CardList abstraction is designed around the app's real variation and stretches well; some duplication in detail-page boilerplate and the mixed details.tsx file hold it back.

findings.issue: Pokémon page hardcodes links to /abilities/<name>, so removing or renaming the Abilities feature leaves dead links in an unrelated page.
findings.suggestion: Keep the link, but if the features' lifecycles are expected to diverge, note the coupling or centralize ability URLs beside the ability views.

findings.issue: Route URL patterns are inlined as template literals in five places (also pokemon.tsx:178, details.tsx:86, details.tsx:146, home.tsx:19), so any route rename is a cross-file grep-and-edit.
findings.suggestion: Add small url helpers (e.g. speciesUrl(name), typeUrl(name)) next to the routes or in data.ts and use them everywhere.

findings.issue: API records are typed 'any' throughout the views (loadMoves, loadMove's move fields, typesByPokemonId's record), so the data contracts the components rely on are implicit and edits are guesswork despite strict tsconfig.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API records actually consumed (Pokemon, Move, Type) in data.ts and type the loaders with them.

findings.issue: One file holds three unrelated resources (moves, abilities, types), hurting locality for resource-scoped changes and leaving no obvious slot for a new resource like Items.
findings.suggestion: Split into move.tsx, ability.tsx, type.tsx alongside the existing home.tsx/pokemon.tsx convention.

findings.issue: The effect-text fallback chain (englishEffect || latestFlavorText || Dash) is duplicated between MovePage and AbilityPage.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared effectText(resource) helper in data.ts.

findings.issue: mainTypes fetches all 18 full type records and typeLabels rebuilds a Map from them; label lookups are then threaded through many call sites as a parameter.
findings.suggestion: Cache the label map once (module-level memo over the existing API cache) or derive labels lazily per view.

findings.issue: The onError handler inlines an error-page fragment instead of a view component, so a future redesign of error pages misses it.
findings.suggestion: Move the error markup into views/components.tsx beside NotFound.

summary: This is a well-layered, easy-to-change small app: data source and caching live in one module, sprite rendering and card lists share single seams, and the Card abstraction models real variation without flags. The main editability costs are duplicated route URL literals across five files, pervasive 'any' typing of API records, and a details.tsx that bundles three unrelated resources plus an ability feature that leaks a hard link into the Pokémon page. I'd merge it with the low-severity cleanups queued as follow-ups.
